text:
I looked at the corpse, his swift visible order
+and the slowest disorder of his soul;
+I saw him survive; within his mouth
+the broken-off age of two mouths.
+They shouted his number to him: pieces.
+They shouted his love to him: better had he not!
+They shouted his bullet to him: dead as well!
+
+And his digestive order held
+while his soul’s disorder, behind, held on in vain.
+They left him and heard him, and it is then
+that the corpse
+almost lived in secret, for an instant;
+but they listened to him mentally—and dates!
+wept into his ear—and dates as well!

translation.title: I Looked at the Corpse
translation.editorial_note: The body’s clinical order is set against the soul’s radically slowed disorder; the repeated dates remain unexplained verdicts rather than being normalized into chronology.
